\chapter{Review --- The Three Forms Side by Side}
\label{ch:review-ar-singular}
\hlchaptermodality{19}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can hold all three singular -ar forms at once and choose between them without stopping.}

The first paradigm table in the book, arriving only after all three of its cells are owned.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[Practice]{Review — the three forms, side by side}

\label{lesson:ES-C06-ar-presente}



\begin{quote}
Nothing new in this chapter. Not one word. Say the three forms you already have, in any order they come.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: the table you have earned}]
Three chapters, one form each. Now — and only now — they are worth seeing together:

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{who} & \textbf{ending} & \textbf{\emph{hablar} $\to$} & \textbf{meaning} \\
\midrule
I & \textbf{-o} & \textbf{hablo} & I speak \\
tú & \textbf{-as} & \textbf{hablas} & you speak (a friend) \\
él · ella · usted & \textbf{-a} & \textbf{habla} & he/she speaks · you speak (polite) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

A table like this one at the \emph{start} would have been three things at once and you would have memorised it. Arriving here, it is a picture of something you can already do.

\textbf{This is the whole engine.} Every regular \textbf{-ar} verb in Spanish — and there are thousands — runs on these three endings. You have not learned one verb. You have learned the pattern that fits all of them.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item Say what \textbf{you} do — \emph{hablo}.
  \item Ask or state what a \textbf{friend} does — \emph{hablas}.
  \item Say what \textbf{someone else} does, or address someone \textbf{politely} — \emph{habla}.
  \item Do all three \textbf{without a pronoun}, because the ending carries it.
\end{itemize}
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item all three in order — \textquotedblleft{}hablo, hablas, habla\textquotedblright{}
  \item them out of order, as prompted: \emph{she} · \emph{I} · \emph{a friend} · \emph{politely}
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:} Until the ending arrives before you have to think about it.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Three endings — name them. (\textbf{-o}, \textbf{-as}, \textbf{-a}.) How many regular \emph{-ar} verbs does this pattern fit? (\textbf{All of them}.) Next chapter you will not learn anything either — you will \emph{use} this to say something you actually mean.
\end{tcolorbox}
